speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) what is the Public Service’s response to the latest TAFEP guideline on mental health declaration as a discriminatory practice; (b) which Government agencies are still asking for this declaration from job applicants; (c) how many applicants who declared their mental health condition have joined the Public Service and how many have not; and (d) what is the Public Service’s workplace mental health and fair employment strategy in the hiring and support of persons with mental health conditions and the fostering of a mental-health friendly environment for all employees.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our public agencies provide support at different levels to our officers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Alternative work arrangements, such as part-time work, can be explored between officers with mental health conditions and their supervisors to better manage their condition or recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, we understand that this alone is not enough.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We need to establish higher awareness of mental health and a strong culture of peer support.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Therefore, we are promoting wider training of our managers and human resource officers to extend appropriate care, when necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We tap on training programmes, such as the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB's) Management Training workshop, to equip managers with skills to detect early signs of distress and to support employees in managing them.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Several public agencies have also built up a network of officers to provide first-in-line peer support to their colleagues who are in distress.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For instance, the National Council of Social Service has a group of Wellness Warriors to provide a listening ear to their colleagues who need one.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our officers' overall well-being is important to us.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: PSD seeks to continually learn and enhance our initiatives to enhance workplace mental health.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Therefore, we welcome and participate in the Workwell Leaders Workgroup, which is a useful platform to learn best practices.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: PSD will continue working with our public agencies to strengthen a caring workplace culture for all.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I appreciate the Minister's assurance because, as the largest employer and given that one in seven Singaporeans has a mental health condition in their lifetime, we would not want to turn Singaporeans away who want to serve in the Public Service.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I just want to read this from someone who wrote to me: "I tried to register as a relief teacher with the Ministry of Education (MOE) but was rejected just because I have a history of depression." Now, I understand, obviously, it is very textured.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But I just want to ask the Minister how are we ensuring that all Ministries and agencies will adhere to the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) guidelines.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, can the Minister also share if the Government allows for medical claims for psychiatric treatment and if mental health leave is given for Government employees.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: If not, are there plans to do so?
